source_caption:
Edgar Wright and Simon Pegg went to the Brixton Police Station, hoping to get some anecdotes from serving officers, and they even offered to take them to the pub. However, every officer refused to speak to them. It soon turned out that the liaison officer had wrongly told his colleagues that Wright and Pegg were journalists. The liaison officer has never been forgiven.
-

Dir. Edgar Wright

source_details.title: Hot Fuzz
source_details.synopsis: Hot Fuzz is a 2007 British action comedy film directed by Edgar Wright and written by Wright and Simon Pegg. Pegg stars as Nicholas Angel, an elite police officer who is reassigned to a West Country village and investigates a series of gruesome deaths. Nick Frost co-stars as Police Constable Danny Butterman, Angel's partner. Hot Fuzz is the second and most commercially successful film in the Three Flavours Cornetto trilogy, following Shaun of the Dead and followed by The World's End. More than 100 action films were used as inspiration for the script.
